<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915617_theRebbe_822__p006">
  <section v="15">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>There are two modes in the Supernal Daas: externally, the lower is nullified, but internally, it exists to reveal Ein Sof's infinitude.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="1">that this is the case regarding the Supernal Daas,</t>
    <t s="2">which has two modes.</t>
    <t s="3">For in its externality, it appears that this lower [entity] is not, because the lower, from its own perspective, is naught and considered nothing,</t>
    <t s="4">and in its internality, this lower [entity] is, in order to reveal that Ein Sof is below, even to the lowest extreme without end.</t>
    <t s="5">And through the Supernal Daas being drawn into the lower Daas and uniting with it, its internality is revealed.</t>
    <t s="6">And this is the case regarding miracles and nature,</t>
    <t s="7">that through the drawing of miracles into the world,</t>
    <t s="8">(nature)</t>
    <t s="9">their internality is revealed,</t>
    <t s="10">that this—that in the conduct above nature, the creations do not occupy space—is because it so arose in His will, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is "Blessed is He who performed miracles for our forefathers,"</t>
    <t s="12">"for our forefathers" in the plural,</t>
    <t s="13">for the elevation and ascent through the performance of miracles</t>
    <t s="14">is both in Binah</t>
    <t s="15">(the root of nature)</t>
    <t s="16">and in Chochmah</t>
    <t s="17">(the root above nature),</t>
    <t s="18">that both matters are not for their own sake, but in order to reveal that Ein Sof is above without end and below without limit.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="16">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The union of nature and the supernatural is possible because within nature itself there is an aspect of self-nullification, as seen in the formation of creatures from the will.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, in order for the union of the two matters to be possible—</t>
    <t s="2">that within the nature of the world</t>
    <t s="3">[in which it is emphasized that the world is a reality,</t>
    <t s="4">for that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts every creature according to its nature indicates that in this conduct, the creatures occupy space]</t>
    <t s="5">there will be the revelation of that which is above nature</t>
    <t s="6">[in which the self-nullification of the world is emphasized,</t>
    <t s="7">for that the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts the world according to His will and not according to the nature and characteristics of the creatures indicates that in this conduct, the creatures do not occupy space]—</t>
    <t s="8">it is through that within nature itself there is the aspect of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="9">And as explained above</t>
    <t s="10">(in the discourse "Patah Eliyahu"),</t>
    <t s="11">that the fact that the form of the creatures was not specified in the Ten Utterances,</t>
    <t s="12">and the coming into being of the form in each creature is from the aspect of the will,</t>
    <t s="13">indicates the self-nullification of the world,</t>
    <t s="14">for the coming into being from the will,</t>
    <t s="15">its meaning is</t>
    <t s="16">(not that creatures come into being, but rather)</t>
    <t s="17">that through the coming into being, the will is fulfilled.</t>
    <t s="18">And through the coming into being of the form in every creature,</t>
    <t s="19">for the intention in the form of the creature is</t>
    <t s="20">(both for its physical image and)</t>
    <t s="21">also for its nature and characteristics,</t>
    <t s="22">was from the aspect of the will,</t>
    <t s="23">behold, this emphasizes that the essence of nature</t>
    <t s="24">(in its internality)</t>
    <t s="25">is that through it, the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, is fulfilled.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="17">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The self-nullification within nature applies to both the vitality of the world and its creation ex nihilo, as each reveals dependence on the divine will.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it was explained above</t>
    <t s="1">(in the discourse "Patah Eliyahu")</t>
    <t s="2">that according to the interpretation that "nature" (teva) is from the term "coin" (matbea), that the Holy One, blessed be He, imprinted every person with the seal of Adam the First,</t>
    <t s="3">there the term "nature" refers to the vitality of the world,</t>
    <t s="4">and according to the interpretation that "nature" is a borrowed term for anything not based on reason and intellect,</t>
    <t s="5">there the term "nature" refers to the coming into being of the world from nothing to something,</t>
    <t s="6">for creation yesh me'ayin</t>
    <t s="7">(unlike the matter of vitality)</t>
    <t s="8">is above intellect.</t>
    <t s="9">And it may be said,</t>
    <t s="10">that the self-nullification within nature pertains to both matters.</t>
    <t s="11">For the self-nullification that relates to the vitality of the world is revealed in the self-nullification of the form of the creatures, because the form of the creatures is a vessel for the vitality and soul within them</t>
    <t s="12">(as above in the discourse "Patah Eliyahu"),</t>
    <t s="13">and the self-nullification that relates to the coming into being of the world is revealed in that the coming into being of yesh me'ayin has no place in the intellect.</t>
    <t s="14">For this—that there is no place in the intellect for the coming into being of yesh me'ayin—</t>
    <t s="15">indicates that from the perspective of the world's definition, there is no place for its coming into being,</t>
    <t s="16">and that the world came into being is only from the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
